column12: In the context of coronavirus (COVID-19): the period of time between infection and the appearance of symptoms of the disease.

column14: In the context of the coronavirus (COVID-19): the practice of restricting the movement of healthy people who may have been exposed to the virus to see if they become ill.
column15: In the context of the coronavirus (COVID-19): to restrict the movement of healthy people who may have been exposed to the virus to see if they become ill.
column16: Short for "National Institutes of Health Agency": the primary US government agency responsible for biomedical and public health research; part of the United States Department of Health and Human Services.
column17: In the context of coronavirus (COVID-19): being within a close distance (1-2m) of another person, not necessarily having actual physical contact. Close contact is one possible way for the virus to spread from person to person.
column18: In the context of coronavirus (COVID-19): the process of the virus spreading from person to person.

column20: In the context of coronavirus (COVID-19): a place where people can be tested for the virus.
column21: In the context of the coronavirus (COVID-19): to infect new people, in a particular area or globally.
